name: Fronius Primo
fit: A single-phase home choosing ordinary rooftop solar, with a separate battery decision later.
why: Two independent solar inputs let the installer manage panels on different roof directions. Solar.web monitoring can show how the system is generating.
check: Primo and Primo GEN24 are different products. Ordinary Primo has no direct battery connection and does not provide blackout power by itself. A later battery needs a separately compatible system. Check the fan's location and the exact Australian model's written warranty.

name: Fronius Primo GEN24 Plus
fit: A single-phase home planning solar and a matched battery together.
why: The Plus version combines solar and battery connections. Its PV Point offers a separate emergency outlet, while a complete backup installation can supply selected household circuits.
check: PV Point is a dedicated outlet, not automatic whole-home backup. Full Backup needs a supported inverter variant, compatible battery, switching equipment and the right circuit design. Confirm the quote says GEN24 Plus, since ordinary GEN24 and later battery activation differ. Check the exact model and written warranty.

name: Enphase IQ8
fit: A roof where separately managed panels and panel-level monitoring are useful, such as several roof faces.
why: Each panel has its own small inverter rather than sharing one central solar inverter. A compatible IQ Gateway provides system monitoring; the layout can be designed around individual panels.
check: IQ8AC, IQ8HC and other IQ8 variants must match the panel's electrical limits. IQ8 alone does not give an Australian home blackout power: the backed-up system needs a compatible battery, system controller and circuit design. Confirm the complete equipment list and each component's Australian warranty.
